summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).
Chris Clark works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney by 2015, where he was attested as an honorary associate in 2019.

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, earning a Magister under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, alongside teachers Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (~1999–2003) and has served as a fellow at the Asiatic Society and Associate Professor at the College of Charleston (~2006).
Christian Gottlob Heyne was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Leipzig University (~1748–1752), he held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1812.

Christian Haskett is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned an MA advised by Robert A. F. Thurman and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), later holding a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Wesleyan University and Columbia University (PhD ~1992–1999 under Robert A. F. Thurman) and has served as Professor at the University of Chicago since circa 2003.

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen was a scholar in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his studies at the University of Marburg (~1808–1809) and the University of Göttingen (~1809–1812).

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Wilhelm Schlegel at the University of Bonn (~1823–1827). He served at Bonn as an außerordentlicher Professor (1830) and ordentlicher Professor of Old Indian Language and Literature (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia University (~1997–2002), subsequently holding posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~2002–2007) and the University of Washington (professor from ~2007).
Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his Magister and PhD from the University of Vienna. He has held posts at the University of Vienna, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and the Rubin Museum of Art.

Christian Matthias Boehm is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of John T. Carpenter (attested 2005).
Christian Wittern is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who has held academic posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993 as Professor, and 2008) and Hanazono University (attested 2011).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and has served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kristofer Schipper and served at the CNRS as a researcher (1989–1995) and Director of Research (attested 2006–2014), as well as Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

Christoph Anderl specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (-1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1997–2003) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983), completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University by 2004 and has held posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto as Assistant Professor.

Christoph Harbsmeier is a Sinologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen. He was a professor at the University of Oslo (~1985–2016) and served as advisory professor at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal Universities (attested 2001).
